text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigeria's electoral commission has set July 31 as the date for local government byelections in 11 of the 24 states where they need to be held, following inconclusive results in March.
- Government has agreed to build a second national theatre in Abuja. A piece of land in the capital has been approved for the project.
- Nigerian Telecommunications is making moves to check discrepancies in its billing system, which have led to disputes with customers.
- Fears have been raised that major shipping companies are abandoning Nigerian to old and poorly maintained ships because of the drop in the volume of trade.
- Farmers argue that if money spent importing rice was invested in them then the quality of local rice would meet international standards.
- Nigerian Customs Service and vehicle licensing offices are trading accusations over who is to blame for the fraudulent registration of imported vehicles on which duty has never been paid.
- Petroleum marketers allay fears of a fresh fuel crisis after the appearance of long queues at filling stations over the weekend.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha says government will only fund projects that can expand Nigeria's revenue base.
- Nigerian companies face mounting bank debts and declining sales, a Guardian survey shows.
- Total Nigeria may be heading for a clash with Nigerian shareholders over its sale of a 51 percent stake in the Nigerian Gas Cylinders Manufacturing Company.
- An upward review of fringe benefits for civil servants, believed to have been approved by government, may cost the treasury 11.8 billion naira every year.
- United Nations Development Programme says Nigeria cannot meet targets for education, health, family planning, water and housing by the year 2000.
